preamble: Vocalization of a voiced labiodental consonant to the high back rounded vowel [u]. Friction and the labiodental contact are given up, while labiality and voicing are kept. In Slovene, /ʋ/ at the start of a syllable before a consonant is pronounced by many speakers as a full syllabic [u] (vsi [uˈsî] 'all'), and next to a vowel it is a non-syllabic [u̯]. In the history of English, the Old English voiced fricative [v] between vowels (spelled f) vocalized to the u-offglide of a diphthong after syncope, as in hafoc > Middle English havek ~ hauk > hawk.

examples.note: Syllable-initial /ʋ/ before a consonant becomes a full vowel [u] for some speakers. Others keep it consonantal by labializing the next consonant ([ˈʷsî]). Next to a vowel, /ʋ/ is pronounced as bilabial [u̯] and forms a diphthong.
After the unstressed vowel was lost, the intervocalic voiced fricative [v] vocalized to [u], giving the diphthong au that underlies Modern English hawk.
